clue.text: Tablet providing uplift and stimulus

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the pieces up means reading them from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a tablet is a pill
providing as a conjunction means if

explanation.surface: A pill that gives a lift and a stimulus to the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplift' turns PILL IF upside down in the column, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or spur, a direct synonym of stimulus.

clue.text: Continue to be stubborn, so cane produced?

definitions.meaning: to persist obstinately, refusing to give in
a cane or stick brought out into view, read literally

explanation.surface: Someone stays obstinate, and so the punishing cane comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick it out is an idiom for persisting doggedly; read literally, a stick has been put out.

clue.text: Good health shown by professional model

parts.note: pro is the short form of professional
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A professional model raising a glass to good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a Latin-derived drinking toast wishing good health, like cheers.

clue.text: Concern of an eleven yet to be organised

parts.note: taken as written
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, also a cricket or football team

indicators.note: letters that are yet to be organised still need arranging into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A team captain worries that his eleven still needs organising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven' suggests a sports side (XI); 'to be organised' rearranges XI and YET into XIETY, after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety is worry or unease, which is what concern means as a noun.

clue.text: Annoyed about article, became abusive

indicators.note: riled goes about, round the outside of, the article letter

parts.note: riled means annoyed
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by a newspaper article started hurling abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly or rant abusively, so railed means became abusive.

clue.text: Poor diet on Asian vessel?

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship

explanation.surface: Sailors on an Eastern ship eat badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk food is unhealthy processed eating, a poor diet; the junk is also a boat.

clue.text: No beer left? That's the limit!

definitions.meaning: the last of the bitter, the end of a pint of bitter beer
the furthest point, the very last extreme

explanation.surface: A drinker finds the pub has run dry and declares it unbearable.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter end is an idiom for the uttermost limit; literally it is the end of the bitter.

clue.text: A huge development in the city

indicators.note: a development of the letters is them changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A huge building development is going on in town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hague is the Dutch seat of government, a city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Worn at funerals and clubs, for example

definitions.meaning: in cards, clubs and spades are the dark-coloured suits

explanation.surface: Mourners and club members both dress in sombre style.
explanation.definitionFit: A black suit is mourning wear; in cards clubs is a black suit, alongside spades.

clue.text: Southern stretch of water to satisfy one's desire

parts.note: a lake is an inland stretch of water

explanation.surface: A southern lake is where one goes to quench a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake is to quench a thirst or appetite, that is, satisfy a craving.

clue.text: A light headband

parts.note: a ring of light shown round a saint's head, like a glowing band

explanation.surface: A flimsy band worn around the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light pictured around a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Solicitor to go to work — or decide not to?

indicators.note: the solicitor is told to go to, follow on from, the work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a tout is one who solicits custom

explanation.surface: Should a lawyer start the job or choose to withdraw?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but it is a tout, someone who touts for business.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part, to decide not to.

clue.text: A gin before opening may let an actor down

parts.note: a gin is an animal trap, a snare
a door is an opening into a room

explanation.surface: A drink before the show's opening night may ruin a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a gin trap; the trapdoor in a stage floor lowers an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage trapdoor drops a performer below the boards, literally letting them down.

clue.text: It may be charged or one may be charged with it

definitions.meaning: an electric cell that stores power and is recharged

definitions.text: one may be charged with it
definitions.meaning: the crime of assault and ..., an offence a person is charged with

explanation.surface: Something gets charged, and someone may be charged for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery stores electric charge; battery is also the legal offence of unlawful physical attack.

clue.text: New Year, when there's a situation of uncertainty

indicators.note: new letters means a fresh arrangement of the ones given

explanation.surface: The new year is a time when things are uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Year' reads as a festival but 'New' signals rearranging YEAR WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anywhere names no particular location, a place left unspecified and so uncertain.

clue.text: Rush animal from below

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards turns the word backwards

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature dashing up out of the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a marsh plant, and a reed is a similar waterside plant.

clue.text: Trust company wrongly fined

indicators.note: something done wrongly is set out of its proper order

explanation.surface: A trust company has been fined unjustly.
explanation.definitionFit: To confide is to put trust in someone, telling them secrets.

clue.text: Below standard tirade is outrageous

indicators.note: in a down clue the tirade sits below the standard

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A substandard rant is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below standard' looks like 'substandard' but it places one piece under the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaringly offensive, conspicuously shocking, which is outrageous.

clue.text: Elaborate blossom

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to work out in more detail
as a verb, to grow and flourish

explanation.definitionFit: To develop an idea is to expand on it; a person or plant can develop, that is grow and bloom.

clue.text: Look at coin with lens

parts.note: to eye is to look at
a piece is a coin, as in a fifty-pence piece

explanation.surface: Studying a coin through a magnifying glass.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyepiece is the lens you look through at the top of a microscope or telescope.

clue.text: Girl on cricket side is not a true member

parts.note: Peg is a girl's name, short for Margaret
the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the side of the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: A girl on the cricket team is not a real member of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side, also called on side, is the half of a cricket field behind a batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg leg is a wooden artificial leg, so not a true limb; member here means limb.

clue.text: Get the game moving and thrash

definitions.meaning: on a shoot, beaters drive game birds up into the air

explanation.surface: Kick off the match and hammer the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaters beat up game birds for the guns; to beat up someone is to give them a thrashing.

clue.text: Circumvent with the aid of permit

parts.note: by means using, as in by hand
a pass is a permit

explanation.surface: Getting round restrictions with a permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass is to go around something, avoiding it, which is to circumvent.

clue.text: Ruined but not executed

explanation.surface: Ruined, but at least not put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Undone means brought to ruin, and also simply not done or carried out.

clue.text: Skirt hem raised above the knee

indicators.note: a hem is the bottom edge of a garment, so the skirt's hem is its final letter

parts.note: something raised is high

explanation.surface: A short skirt with its hem lifted over the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hem' takes the end letter of 'Skirt', T, and HIGH follows; the whole clue reads as a hemline.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the part of the leg lying above the knee, between it and the hip.

clue.text: Reckless person's crazy road speed

indicators.note: crazy letters are jumbled out of their sensible order

explanation.surface: A reckless driver's mad speed on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a bold, reckless outlaw ready to take any risk.

clue.text: Caught fish — put right in this

definitions.text: Caught fish — put right in this

indicators.note: the right letter is put in amid the other letters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A caught fish should be placed properly in this basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which anglers put their catch.

clue.text: Agreeing to study issue with worker

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn
a son is issue, offspring
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: Agreeing to study the matter with a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonant with means in agreement with, consistent, so agreeing.
